verdict.summary: You can build a public OAuth app for each customer's Linear workspace. OAuth app setup is self-serve. Directory distribution needs Linear approval. Build a useful integration backed by a formal company, then submit it for directory review.
verdict.activeEffort: 1–3 days, mostly building OAuth, secure token storage, and agent event handling
verdict.waitTime: Unknown: no official or community figure found
verdict.mainGate: You need Linear directory review only if you want the agent listed in Linear's Integration Directory.

recommendation.text: Create a public OAuth app. Add actor=app so the agent appears as its own workspace participant. Use the Integration Directory for broad agent distribution.

essentials.text: Use PKCE with S256 and validate state. Verify webhook HMAC signatures against the raw body. Reject webhook events older than one minute.

sources.quote: Linear supports the PKCE flow . To use this flow, you’ll need to include two additional parameters as part of your /authorize request:
This header contains a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body contents, signed using the webhook’s signing secret.
We recommend that you verify it’s within a minute of the time your system sees it to guard against replay attacks.

requests.text: Send the user here and verify the returned state matches RANDOM_STATE.

sources.quote: GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize HTTP/1.1

scope 
 (required) Comma separated list of scopes:

state 
 (optional, recommended ) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied.

code_challenge 
 (required) Code challenge you generated
 code_challenge_method 
 (required) Either plain or S256

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Exchange the authorization code using the verifier generated for the PKCE challenge.

sources.quote: POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token HTTP/1.1
Pass parameters in body as URL-encoded form submission , where the Content-Type header must be application/x-www-form-urlencoded .

code_verifier 
 (required) The code verifier for the PKCE request that you originally generated before the authorization request
 grant_type=authorization_code 
 (required)

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens

requests.text: Save both replacement tokens returned by every successful refresh.

sources.quote: POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token HTTP/1.1
Pass parameters in body as URL-encoded form submission , where the Content-Type header must be application/x-www-form-urlencoded .

refresh_token 
 (required) Refresh token from the previous step
 grant_type=refresh_token 
 (required)
If your access token was generated using PKCE, you can simply pass client_id as a parameter.

requests.label: Refresh the access token

sources.quote: POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/revoke HTTP/1.1
To revoke a user’s access, call the revocation endpoint and include the token to be revoked in the token form field of the request body.
If available, include token_type_hint ( access_token or refresh_token ) to help the server identify the token.

detail.text: Expose a public HTTPS webhook endpoint. Verify the HMAC over the raw request body with a timing-safe comparison. Check that the event timestamp is within one minute to protect against replay attacks.

log.name: read
detail: OAuth2 applications should be managed in a dedicated workspace because each admin user will have access. | quote: "It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access."
Create an OAuth2 application in Linear and configure its redirect callback URLs. | quote: "Create a new OAuth2 Application and configure the redirect callback URLs to your application."
The authorization endpoint is `https://linear.app/oauth/authorize`. | quote: "GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize HTTP/1.1"
Authorization-code requests require `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code`, and `scope`. | quote: "client_id (required) Client ID provided when you create the OAuth2 Application"

The default `read` scope always applies; available scopes include `write`, `issues:create`, `comments:create`, `timeSchedule:write`, and `admin`. | quote: "read - (Default) Read access for the user’s account. This scope will always be present."

The `admin` scope provides full admin-level access and should only be requested when absolutely necessary. | quote: "admin - Full access to admin level endpoints. You should never ask for this permission unless it’s absolutely needed"
The `state` parameter is optional but recommended to prevent CSRF attacks. | quote: "state (optional, recommended ) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied."

Linear supports PKCE; authorization requests require `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method`, using either `plain` or `S256`. | quote: "Linear supports the PKCE flow . To use this flow, you’ll need to include two additional parameters as part of your /authorize request:"

After authorization, Linear redirects to a callback URL configured in the OAuth2 application. | quote: "Once the user approves your application they will be redirected back to your application, with the OAuth authorization code in the URL params."
The returned `state` must match the original value; mismatches must not be trusted. | quote: "If the values do not match, the request should not be trusted."
The token exchange endpoint is `https://api.linear.app/oauth/token`. | quote: "POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token HTTP/1.1"

Authorization-code token requests use URL-encoded form data with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. | quote: "Pass parameters in body as URL-encoded form submission , where the Content-Type header must be application/x-www-form-urlencoded ."

The authorization-code exchange requires the same `redirect_uri` used in the authorization request, plus `client_id`, `client_secret`, and `grant_type=authorization_code`. | quote: "redirect_uri (required) Same redirect URI which you used in the previous step"
PKCE token exchange requires `code_verifier`; `client_secret` is optional. | quote: "client_secret (optional) Application’s client secret"

Authorization-code access tokens last 24 hours by default and are renewed by exchanging the refresh token for a new token pair. | quote: "Authorization code user or app 24 hours by default Exchange the refresh token for a new token pair."

Each refresh token expires 30 days after issuance; successful refreshes rotate both tokens and provide a new 30-day refresh-token lifetime. | quote: "Each refresh token expires 30 days after issuance. A successful refresh returns a new access token and refresh token, with a new 30-day refresh-token lifetime."
API requests do not extend access-token or refresh-token lifetimes. | quote: "API requests do not extend either lifetime."

Returned credentials should be saved together, and refreshes should be coordinated across processes sharing an authorization. | quote: "Save the returned credentials together and coordinate refreshes across processes sharing an authorization."
If a refresh token expires or is revoked, authorization must be completed again. | quote: "If the current refresh token expires or is revoked, complete authorization again."

If a successful refresh response is lost, the same refresh token can be retried within 30 minutes to recover replacement credentials. | quote: "If a refresh succeeds but its response is lost, retry with the same refresh token within 30 minutes of the original successful refresh to recover the replacement credentials."

detail: OAuth app manifests define a Linear OAuth app as structured data, supporting reproducible hosted-platform setup and pre-populated configurations for self-hosted or open-source projects. | quote: "OAuth app manifests let developers define a Linear OAuth app as structured data instead of filling the form manually."
Linear supports URL parameters and JSON manifests as equivalent configuration formats. | quote: "Linear supports two equivalent formats:"
URL parameters can open a pre-populated OAuth app creation page. | quote: "Use URL parameters when you want to send someone directly to a pre-filled app setup page."

JSON manifests are intended for storing, validating, sharing, or programmatically generating app configuration. | quote: "Use the JSON manifest format when you want to store the configuration in a file, validate it locally, or generate it programmatically."
The app creation page accepts configuration through URL parameters at the workspace-agnostic endpoint. | quote: "https://linear.app/settings/api/applications/new"
App distribution can be private to the current workspace or public and installable by other workspaces; private is the default. | quote: "Allowed values: private , public"

The JSON manifest is the canonical, versioned representation of the OAuth app configuration. | quote: "The JSON manifest format is the canonical, versioned representation of the same OAuth app configuration."

The published JSON Schema can be referenced for local editor and CI validation. | quote: "Developers can reference it from the $schema field so editors and CI tooling can validate the manifest locally."

Repeated query parameters represent array values such as redirect URIs, grant types, and webhook resource types. | quote: "Repeated query parameters are used for array values such as oauth.redirect_uris , oauth.grant_types , and webhook.resourceTypes ."

Unsupported query parameters are ignored, and a JSON manifest takes precedence over dot-notation parameters when both are provided. | quote: "If both dot-notation parameters and a manifest query parameter are provided, the JSON manifest takes precedence."
OAuth redirect URIs must be absolute HTTP or HTTPS URLs; one to 32 unique values are supported. | quote: "Minimum items: 1"
Multiple redirect URIs can be supplied by repeating the redirect URI parameter. | quote: "Repeat this parameter to provide multiple values."
Supported grant types are authorization_code and client_credentials, with authorization_code always required. | quote: "Allowed values: authorization_code , client_credentials"
Authorization-code grants use refresh tokens, while client-credentials grants do not. | quote: "Authorization-code grants use refresh tokens; client-credentials grants do not."
Grant types configure supported authorization flows, not actors or token lifetimes; refresh_token must not be added. | quote: "Do not add refresh_token to this field."

Scopes are requested in authorization or client-credentials requests rather than declared in the manifest. | quote: "Request scopes in the authorization or client-credentials request, not the manifest."
A JSON manifest must specify schemaVersion, currently 1.0.0. | quote: "Current value: 1.0.0"
Webhooks are optional; enabling them requires an HTTPS URL and resource types. | quote: "Optional webhook configuration for the OAuth app."
Webhook URLs must use HTTPS and cannot target loopback hosts, private-network hosts, or linear.app. | quote: "The host must not be a loopback host, private-network host, or linear.app"
Webhook resource types are repeatable query parameters or string arrays in JSON and must contain at least one unique value when configured. | quote: "Minimum items: 1 when webhook.url is set"

Requests are associated with the authenticated user, which means all requests by the same user share the same quota even when using different API keys."
OAuth apps are limited to 5,000 requests per user or app user per hour. | quote: "OAuth App 5,000 User (or App User) 1 hour"

Unauthenticated requests are limited to 600 requests per hour per originating IP address. | quote: "When making unauthenticated requests, you are limited to 600 requests per hour . These requests are associated with the originating IP address instead of the user making the request."

Global request-limit headers report the limit, remaining requests, and reset time in UTC epoch milliseconds. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Requests-Reset The time at which the current rate limit window resets in UTC epoch milliseconds ."

Some queries and mutations have lower, endpoint-specific request limits, with potentially different windows. | quote: "Some queries and mutations have individual request rate limits that are lower than the global request limit. When one of these limits is hit, the Linear API will send the same response as described in Handling rate limited errors ."
Endpoint-specific limits provide limit, remaining, reset, and endpoint-name headers. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Name The name of the endpoint that was rate limited."

API-key requests are limited to 3,000,000 complexity points per user per hour, shared across API keys. | quote: "Requests authenticated using an API key can request up to 3,000,000 points per hour . Requests are associated with the authenticated user, which means all requests by the same user share the same quota even when using different API keys."
OAuth apps are limited to 2,000,000 complexity points per user or app user per hour. | quote: "OAuth app 2,000,000 User (or App User) 1 hour"

Unauthenticated requests are limited to 100,000 complexity points per originating IP address per hour. | quote: "Unauthenticated requests are limited to 100,000 points per hour . These requests are associated with the originating IP address instead of the user making the request."

Complexity-limit headers report query complexity, the hourly limit, remaining points, and reset time. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Complexity-Remaining The number of points of API request complexity remaining in the current rate limit window."

A single query may not exceed 10,000 complexity points. | quote: "We also enforce a maximum complexity of a single query at any time to 10,000 points . Your query will always get rejected if it exceeds that."

Complexity is calculated as 0.1 point per property, 1 point per object, and connection child complexity multiplied by pagination; the result is rounded up. | quote: "Each property is 0.1 point, each object is 1 point and any connection multiplies its children’s points based on the given pagination argument, or the default 50. The score is then rounded up to the nearest integer."

Free and Basic plans receive standard limits; Business receives 2× standard limits; Enterprise receives 5× standard limits. | quote: "Free, Basic Standard limits Business 2x standard limits Enterprise 5x standard limits"

Workspace-level OAuth apps using Actor Authorization may receive further dynamic rate-limit increases based on paid users. | quote: "we dynamically increase rate limits further for workspace level OAuth apps using Actor Authorization based on number of paid users in that workspace."

Requests exceeding a rate limit return HTTP 429 and a GraphQL error with code RATELIMITED. | quote: "GraphQL requests that exceed a rate limit return HTTP status code 429 . You can catch these by inspecting the errors field in the response body, which contains the RATELIMITED error code."
The Retry-After header specifies how many seconds to wait before retrying. | quote: "The Retry-After header gives the number of seconds to wait before retrying."

log.name: read
detail: Webhook consumers must use a publicly accessible HTTPS, non-localhost URL. | quote: "It’s available in a publicly accessible HTTPS, non-localhost URL"

Linear recommends securing webhook POST requests by verifying their signature and timestamp, or checking the source IP address. | quote: "You can do this in two ways: verifying the webhook request signature and timestamp, and checking the source IP address."

The `Linear-Signature` header contains a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body, signed with the webhook’s signing secret. | quote: "This header contains a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body contents, signed using the webhook’s signing secret."
The webhook signing secret is available on the webhook’s detail page. | quote: "You can find the signing secret on the webhook’s detail page."

Webhook consumers should verify the `webhookTimestamp` is within one minute to help prevent replay attacks. | quote: "We recommend that you verify it’s within a minute of the time your system sees it to guard against replay attacks."

Signature verification should use the raw request body rather than re-serializing parsed JSON. | quote: "It’s strongly recommended to use raw request body rather than restringifying a parsed JSON body, otherwise the signature may differ."

Verification requires computing an HMAC over the request body with the webhook secret and comparing it with the `Linear-Signature` header. | quote: "To verify the webhook, you need to compute the signature of the request body using the webhook’s signing secret and compare it against the Linear-Signature header."
The example verifies signatures using a timing-safe comparison. | quote: "return crypto.timingSafeEqual(computedSignature, headerSignature);"
The example rejects invalid signatures with HTTP 401. | quote: "if (!verifySignature(req.get(\"linear-signature\"), req.rawBody)) {\n return res.sendStatus(401);\n }"

The example rejects webhook requests older or newer than 60 seconds to prevent replay attacks. | quote: "if (Math.abs(Date.now() - req.body.webhookTimestamp) > 60 * 1000) {\n // Reject any webhooks not within 60 seconds of the current time to prevent replay attacks."

Linear provides a `Linear-Timestamp` header containing the Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the webhook was sent. | quote: "Linear-Timestamp \n A Unix timestamp, in milliseconds, when the webhook was sent."
Linear provides a `Linear-Signature` header described as the HMAC signature of the webhook payload. | quote: "Linear-Signature \n HMAC signature of the webhook payload."

Consumers can additionally validate the webhook source IP against Linear’s documented outbound IP addresses. | quote: "In addition to verifying the signature, you can check the source IP address. Our outbound IP addresses are documented on our Security page ."

log.name: read
detail: Date: July 30, 2025 | quote: "Agent Interaction Guidelines and SDK"

Linear introduced the Agent Interaction Guidelines (AIG), a framework based on learnings from agent partners to help developers design agents that integrate naturally into human workflows. | quote: "These principles and practices help developers design agents that integrate more naturally into human workflows."
AIG is a living document expected to expand as Linear gains practical experience. | quote: "AIG is a living document, and we expect to continually add to it as we learn more in practice."

Linear released the Agent Interaction SDK as a developer preview to structure how agents communicate status and progress, with Linear automatically rendering the appropriate UI. | quote: "The Agent Interaction SDK gives developers a structured way to define how agents communicate status and progress."

Agent delegation now keeps the user as the primary assignee and adds the agent as a contributor working on the user’s behalf. | quote: "When a user delegates an issue to an agent, the user remains the primary assignee, while the agent is added as a contributor working on the user’s behalf."

Agent sessions can communicate whether an agent is actively working, waiting for input, encountering an error, or finished. | quote: "Agents can share a rich status indicating whether they’re actively working, waiting for input, have encountered an error, or completed their work."

Agent activity can expose reasoning steps, tool usage, clarification prompts, and final responses. | quote: "Agents can expose detailed activity like their reasoning steps, tool usage, prompts for clarification, and final responses."

The SDK provides structured, semantic communication of agent behavior and real-time visibility into agent activity within Linear. | quote: "These updates give agent developers a structured, semantic way to communicate agent behavior, while giving users realtime visibility into what agents are doing"

Developers can begin implementing the SDK capabilities immediately. | quote: "The Agent Interaction SDK is available as a developer preview, and developers can start implementing the new capabilities today."

log.name: read
detail: By default, Linear treats the authenticating user as the API actor, so actions appear to come from that user. | quote: "By default all Linear’s API authentication methods treat the authenticating user as the API actor."

OAuth Actor Authorization makes the app—not the user—the actor, after the user authorizes installing the app in the workspace. | quote: "when authenticating this way the user will instead authorize installing the app within the workspace, actions performed with the received OAuth token will come from the app itself."

Enable app-actor authorization by adding the `actor=app` parameter to the OAuth authorization URL. | quote: "To enable the actor authorization, add actor=app parameter to your OAuth authorization URL ."
The actor setting applies to both the authorization and its access token. | quote: "The setting is tied to the authorization and its access token."

In app-actor mode, mutations such as issue creation, comments, and status changes are performed by the app. | quote: "In this mode, all mutations such as creating issues, comments, and status changes will be performed by the app."
Token renewal behavior is unchanged by using `actor=app`. | quote: "Using actor=app changes the identity that performs actions, not how tokens are renewed."

Authorization-code grants require the refresh token to obtain a new access and refresh token pair. | quote: "Authorization-code grants: Use the refresh token to obtain a new access and refresh token pair."

Client-credentials grants do not issue refresh tokens; request a new access token shortly before expiration. | quote: "Client-credentials grants: No refresh token is issued. Request a new access token shortly before the current one expires."

Updating scopes for an authorization-code installation requires repeating the flow with `update_scopes_on_existing_token=true` and requesting all existing plus new scopes. | quote: "repeat the authorization flow with update_scopes_on_existing_token=true . Request the complete scope set: all existing scopes plus any scopes being added."
Scope updates are subject to permission and team-access checks. | quote: "The update is subject to permission and team-access checks."

Exchanging the updated authorization code replaces the installation’s access and refresh tokens, so all processes sharing the credentials must be updated. | quote: "Exchanging the resulting authorization code replaces the installation’s access and refresh tokens, even if the scopes have not changed."

Removing scopes requires revoking the existing authorization and authorizing again with the reduced scope set. | quote: "To remove scopes, revoke the existing authorization and authorize again with the reduced scope set."

Repeating the ordinary installation flow without the update parameter does not change an existing installation’s scopes. | quote: "Repeating the ordinary installation flow without update_scopes_on_existing_token=true does not update an existing installation."

For client credentials, requesting a new scope set revokes existing app-actor tokens for that app in the workspace. | quote: "Adding or removing scopes revokes existing app-actor tokens for that app in the workspace."

Processes sharing a client-credentials app must use the same scope set to avoid token invalidation. | quote: "Processes sharing the app must use the same scope set to avoid invalidating each other’s tokens."

A custom user name and avatar can identify actions performed by the app for users without Linear accounts. | quote: "You can also add an optional user name and avatar to go with the application to have it rendered in User (via Application) format."

The custom display name is set with `createAsUser`, and the avatar URL with `displayIconUrl`, in `issueCreate` or `commentCreate` mutations. | quote: "To set the custom user name, set the createAsUser attribute with the user name and set displayIconUrl with the URL of the avatar in issueCreate or commentCreate mutations:"

The former `actor=application` mode is deprecated in favor of `actor=app`, though existing apps may continue using it. | quote: "actor=application as a mode – this was deprecated in favor of the behavior in actor=app . If your app already uses this option then you can continue to do so."
